candidates.statement: Let us now introduce two adequate spaces of test functions, for which we shall be able to prove speed of convergence estimates.

In the next Section [\[sec:berry\]](#sec:berry){reference-type="ref" reference="sec:berry"}, we shall combine Theorem [\[theorem:tao\]](#theorem:tao){reference-type="ref" reference="theorem:tao"} and the estimates on smooth test distributions given by Proposition [\[prop:zonedistribution\]](#prop:zonedistribution){reference-type="ref" reference="prop:zonedistribution"} to get a Berry--Esseen type bound on the Kolmogorov distances in the setting of mod-$\phi$ convergence.
The maximal value allowed for the exponent $\gamma$ in the size of the zone of control is then $\gamma = 1$, and later we shall encounter many examples of this situation.

Then, we obtain $$d_\mathrm{Kol}(Y_n,Y) \leq \frac{1+\lambda}{\sqrt{2 \pi}}\left(2^\frac{3}{2}\,K_1 + \frac{1}{\sqrt[3]{\pi}\,K }\left(4\sqrt[3]{1+\frac{1}{\lambda}}+3\sqrt[3]{3}\right)\right)\frac{1}{(t_n)^{3/2}}. \label{eq:dKol_MG}$$ In Section [\[sec:dependency\]](#sec:dependency){reference-type="ref" reference="sec:dependency"}, we shall give conditions on cumulants of random variables that lead to mod-Gaussian convergence with a zone of control of size $O(t_n)$ and with index $(3,3)$, so that [\[eq:dKol_MG\]](#eq:dKol_MG){reference-type="eqref" reference="eq:dKol_MG"} holds.
We shall then choose $K$, $K_1$ and $\lambda$ to make the constant in the right-hand side as small as possible. :::
Of course, the advantage of our method is its large range of applications, as we shall see in the next sections.
In the sequel, we shall freely use this small improvement of Corollary [\[cor:Cumulants_Kol\]](#cor:Cumulants_Kol){reference-type="ref" reference="cor:Cumulants_Kol"}. :::
